# Seven Days.
Dear friend, In just seven days, Maryland will be going to the polls on Election Day and deciding whether they will vote for higher taxes, more fees, extreme structural deficits and higher electric bills, or for common sense relief and a stable and prosperous state.

We are now just $18,000 away from our immediate goal for the final cable TV purchase. I have given a matching fund of that amount in order to ensure we cross the finish line strong. But I need your help to match this amount and help me pay for the ads. Thank you to so many who are joining us in this fight.

Remember the Maryland 400. They, the "Old Line," saved General Washington's Army just over a month after the Declaration of Independence was signed, allowing through heroic attack the escape of the entire American Army after being surrounded at the Battle of Long Island.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/5V_D4TIO1dO?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
[Click Here to help us buy Cable TV Ads to Fight for Maryland](https://us.list-manage.com/MbaFbpBqswS?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)

Now in the same spirit of our Maryland 400 - we must stop the disastrous agenda of Absentee Governor Wes Moore. He does not care for you, our children or the future of our State - for him it is all about national appearances and running for president. Consider how he's left Maryland behind:
* highest electric bills in the nation
* second worst economy in the nation
* one of two states with a massive structural deficit
* raised property taxes by valuation increase of 26% last year - more on its way unless we replace him
* $200+ car registration fees
* Key Bridge - not built and not under contract
* Purple Line - doubled in cost to $10 billion and no service yet
* Red Line - a lot of money and not even broken ground
* Triple Crown - excluded from the Thoroughbred Racing
* A-10 Fighter Wing - gone to Michigan Gov. Whitmer
* Commanders - leaving
* Guinness - closed
* Triple A bond rating - gone
* $5 billion Gov Hogan surplus - gone and now we are $3 billion in structural deficit
* 300+ days out of state - nearly a year of his term - running for president

Help me stop him here in Maryland and save our State and nation from his reckless, continued tax and spend policies making us one of the worst economies in the Nation - second worst to be exact.

[Will you chip in to help me reach our Cable TV purchase goal tonight? $176, or in remembrance of our brave Maryland 400, will you donate $400, or even $1776](https://us.list-manage.com/ZB7cHSwcaLN?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)?

The election turnout is currently on par or just about 10% under the Hogan 2018 turnout - a great indicator for us as so many independents and swing democrats are fed up like you with the direction of the state! Wes Moore is losing. With your help we will win.

Thank you.

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Candidate for Governor of Maryland

## Texas Sues OpenAI
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton [sued OpenAI and its CEO](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAQRp9GMyzAHyQg2MRsNt3QaqFRqlAs6Bln3n7LuY9w8-5T53z_HvMDQgzH-hd2NPT2aT7wKhGJMM-EbyjliSWdeEDIa3vBQWWBWXI5MMGZVDNYCi-cO6idWbjTokYjlG65HvUo6s3oxXE1Wmu1H1vnvNW8d4OUtlNeC9XXwdw4waUSgsteN61fFHrULUA_qq6tOo4uUMoNbfiV8vGTXpgbm_Y6mo3oLFX7p5JTJafruhqf3nLY0rNQOu6jSk53VyWn7zu7o9hPFbtBzG5A60msgEf6MBsh7IVBjLiiYxvkne3hSLnU2bjzCjGGMqiq4-sOIX496Lf7vYz8HwAA__-PhYkm), Sam Altman, on Friday, accusing the ChatGPT maker of deceiving Texans about its chatbot's safety and failing to protect children. The [67-page lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAMhp8mbEGJEyAZMtzC1ltvRC6YEimQirilffsTvUe4xbJk6fP__T-X4YIxxe32jSsFfs152OgoiZhpH5heWMqDSr7ThnG_mQM3LlccQEErtZLQDThyfNJgsZrCVU1eVxR0543yzjtdLaG1U-Nab60iB25uvGubFhWMoK0aratiOHFaQae1gsbXZr52NJM3iI3rrBFW0RQ57zUv9Ak1p3d-0l6Pea1SWJjvRZgvAb2A_jiO-o1LzudVQH8KCegf58Cd45joXD8cedrJPz1ZcJWYeMVNamcseLCuXnhN1R6m-xFTiqXthFW3FWP6_Ob_dvYM8BsAAP__iDqAsA), filed in Collin County, says ChatGPT makes "tips on eating disorders, self-harm and mass murder" available to children without age checks or parental consent. It relies on the state's consumer protection law and a 2023 law on kids' online safety. The suit points to [at least eight people](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQRp_GdF75b69x4SIN3U2bEg14DJYMRszsz337iM0jpB7N0Tnfn-_xG0ot-_IbNoz8zm3c8UUVmfEcGd9A9EBqB-5QzsW-YGeaYDTKfEmtpPEjzFyeODroUpxUCrrDqH2wKvSh190ae-8yYnbGee9snr1KGlzIAezk7h67Ei-cVsZrrcw93GyePGYMFuDee2eFU5gKt_PGK36kcv1pTzxvc9u6Glfmg4T9JcwgzLC2lmrZ8ToKM1xsYQathBk-vxIWecCb2y6vNvkvThL8kJxX4OVgmR9YMUl6lLkkJAl7khsQSVpbYzxJmKE7YzpepdZCX144tWxQ6seI_3fJZzR_AwAA__9QmYpu) who used ChatGPT before committing violent acts. It asks a judge to ban minors from using ChatGPT, require outside approval of new models, and set penalties of up to $10,000 per violation. OpenAI said it has [worked with experts](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkM3OpCAQRZ9GdnagUJAFi9m469nO0hRaCgktRmr65-0n9jzCt6y6yck99899umPKad9-44M8v9cy7fSqmZjpnJjeWOtfquWgHdO56RfuXANOIMG0SrZgJ5w5PWnqUCw-yMUpQV5Zp6Ub3KBE9EY77JcQgjXrsPYBAWbTQU8OSQcgkfyFUxKsUhJ6d9NrsLSS04j9YDvddJKWxOW8caRvqTV_ypPO21weIvvIfNRG_2pgbGDkSDHlfGUNjEfJaf5cb5rjXnLZrsMo47Tt2wPfXPb2cmz_S7ZzRN4ObmAUp1-OV8o5VWObTm4PTF-s4J9O9fTwLwAA___TYX-G) to build safeguards and wants rules covering "the entire AI industry--not just one company." Eight other states sued the company earlier this month, and Florida sued in June.
## 13 Charged in Cartel Car Pipeline
U.S. Attorney Justin Simmons on Monday announced [charges against 13 people](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuupDAMQL8mdBnlARNSpNiG7m67JTKJgWhDghJfZvbvV8wv3O5IlnyO_edr_oKYYt5-w4GO3muZM75aQiKsM-EbWvvGVk7MEOumX5CpLTAroZ5cCq7MDJ7ihXMPXXCLCFZ26KSxWtjRjrLb3RLsYM0AEhehwa-iRyFXIzTK8dnrsYvuXieFMlIKNdiHXheDK1oNMIym16wXGCKV-qAdP1Fr-lcurA9fji65nehsTP9iamJq-ntFuAdMTfctTE1LqQErU9PtYWqS4uYPaR5ziJ4wcPD-u2HgZeVUIbezVIp5441Kwswv3KNP2DgVfuA7esjcQyVMt6KrLpyvmFJsT8N6sR0Q0yePfvrWy6n_AQAA___75o0i) accused of driving stolen cars to El Paso and running them across the border to Mexican cartels. The investigation, launched this spring and dubbed Operation Southbound Takedown, recovered 29 vehicles worth more than $1.1 million: 22 in the U.S. and seven in Mexico. [Three vehicles carried explosives](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLtugzAUhp8GNpBvCXjw0IUtXTuiAz4Gq8ZG9gkkb1-RV-j86799P4_xAT74uHzDhoZeLo0RzxKQCPNI-IJSnljSjhF8XuQJkcoEo2Di3nDWiG6EmfyBo4LamolZzWs0vNOS6V73vF6NlpNk0Aul7txa1L3QUoOVbmZOaQe1N1ccZ6LjnImbbqWbOnSoJcCt75SsFEPrKeWWVvyMcuGdDsztnLY6mJVoL5X8qsRQieE8z_aXynaJlRiuP5UY1rRhgGibgvMze3o3lJqMB0JofDywkF-AfIqNxQND2jeMdBnrbOx--hB8uXeVYssGPnyK6b_ADiP-AgAA__9kI4Nt), and their intended use is unknown. Cartels recruited people who could cross the border legally to drive cars stolen from owners and [rental fleets across the Southwest](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE9jMo_sNgw4cLAJ2dt0Q9TYbbBkMKI9f7dfMVd4SQVV0qdP9e9n-sGU0778xY1cfccy7fTiTLXSOVV6I_ODuBy0YzoX88K98owTKLhLrST0E_qanjS12AQ3q2B1Q0731ig72EE3qws9-ehxpg4MGVI22rsfYECIvtMam-QunFbQa62gszcT554iWYPYDX1rRKsopFrOW13pKxXzpzzpvPmyNdmttR4szB8Bo4BxLSXktNM1ChgvtoBRqyuM9CueCwWZdklZHshFIstIgSXjR3ItmXbp8WQZH5QpyI3eyeO3q5RZwNicLhyvlHPiey9atWyY8tel_vbDp4P_AQAA__8QSYeE), investigators said. Eleven of the 13 defendants are U.S. citizens, and two are Mexican nationals. Each defendant faces [up to 10 years](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3S4yAMQE-DOzL8OCEUFNu4-7bd0qOAHDOLIYOUOLn9jnOF7V7xRtLTn5_5B3LJ9f4bNgz8XtpccaeCzNhnxjcQPZHaAyvkfrc7VKYbzEaZi9RKGjdD5PzCeYQhhZtKXg8YtPNW-au_6mEN1zH6883BGZWGS8KIF69cshBjtNrrIYdjnFbGaa3M2Z_scnO4oLcA56sbrRgVpsytn3jF71FL-bQX9lNs21DCyvwgYX8JMwkz7ft-iiXHv2ZtT-JWD0uY6QgTZiotQhFmOnYKM2l18JesjCv0OyaZq4RS8ECKK24ouUnuUOnROkviVrDKF645FiS59LbJJx3Shu8cocoInbGQXDCRJPgIMw09pMeeS8l0cWJU9w1y-Rbw_37-Fcy_AAAA__9TSZqn) in federal prison if convicted. "_These are not isolated property crimes_ ," said Ryan McRae, head of Homeland Security Investigations in El Paso, calling the cars tools for cartels' day-to-day operations.
## UT Athletics Unveils AI Bevo Lab
The University of Texas is [building Bevo Lab](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OwyAUBODT4A4L8A9xQbGNu2y7pfUMzw5aAhY8h-T2q-QKW480-mZ-rssVfPBx_4Y7GnpuaYlYS0AizAvhE0o5saQDI_i8dxUilRUWJdTIpeBKL2DJP3DpoXFmFW6SDRqpp05Ml-kim5txPUjhNAg5Dr2Ug3XrNm6jlStotdqx8eZdJ4XSUgo1TG23rRo3nDqA4aL7jvUCnaeUW7rhB7WFV3pgbm26N8HciI7Cui-mZqbmWmv7-4T4Dpma33uYmtGdFsinyNR8EoezkI_cZgTycecRKwfPj1Qxo-PlSJkKhwjhRd4WHmBlam6ycUf1IfgyataL_Q4-fBD03_MeRv0FAAD__4PRhzg), an artificial intelligence hub that will crunch game film and player data to help Longhorn coaches and athletes train, scout, and game-plan, starting with football. The 25,000-square-foot lab inside Austin's Innovation Tower is backed by Google Cloud, Dell Technologies, and SHI International. Google engineers have already saved coaches more than [15 hours a week](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OtCAYRq8GOww_OkhB8TV287Vbmhd8dUgQDLAye_eb8Ra2f3JynvP1XJ7gg4_7fzjQ1PeWloitBKwV81LxDaV8Y0knRvB5lw1iLRYWwcSDckaFWsBVf-EyQLcay1bNOzRcacn0pCfevQx_KOWYBaeZ0nyTTrNxGARHp_g4KdV588FxJhTnTIy6l5tVuKGWAOOkBkkGhquvKff1hbfUFn7Shbl36eiCedV6FiL_ETETMbfWemdLOVOu5bMgYnYpBNyRbilVCyEQMX9-EjHfOGrxSjSApeDpmRpmXOkOB9IzQIw-7kTMXTbr2XwIvjwUGdh-gA-3Qf1rucuI3wAAAP__3CCE6A) of game prep, the school said. [A data warehouse](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMo9Mm8E4cLAJ2bfphqjBzdBaj41wz9_tV8wVNqtSSU9P9edn-kFOnG-_8U5B3muZMr1qIhE6JqE31vqgWnbKyMfNvjBLnXECA71ujQY34SL8pKnDJobZRN82FFrnrfGDH9pmC30H1vXeuM73cxzwGq3tBw_U-wUiuobDiWsNuLY1cPUXu86OVvIW8Tq4zqrOUGQpx0U2-kqt6VOedFyWcm9S2ET2quwvBaOCMX_2UuWcFIwnWcHYmjNbBWPdyyFVwfjI_KSjsnx0WfWXqlG2RMJL1VL0o5JG1gnns22Udh1p4col6zv-5XzTL5ZNo15Qlk3B2Bwh7i9OiWvvVGdud-T0dZT__fYZ4F8AAAD__58djv0) will pull game film and wearable-tracker readings into one platform, with Google's Gemini fielding coaches' questions. The lab won't call plays, but athletic director Chris Del Conte said it gives Texas "a real chance to improve ourselves." Del Conte [clarified a report](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAUxvGnwQ4DBxUtKLahm223NEc8OGQZMcCM49vfzLzCrb_kn1--f7f5hiGGffuLDzL17dO801ki1Up5rvTGUp5U0kE7hrypE_daFpxBwMCl4KBndDW8aO6wWc0i1kk2ZKSelJjGaZTN3TgvlNOOpsGNKEatZN8P3ntHvtPUQRPMJycFaCkF9FOr_KLJ06QQ-1F3inWC1lBTbuudvigfr_Si3Lr0aKK513oUpv4wsAzseZ4tlWP_jAysSzHSRtynVBeMkYEtNeWLgZ0Z2LAysL2AAXQvGNhvnuPKXcQcfKDCn4U4Bv6fLn5EvHhMpXAfUw4rNtmsxxliDGXQrBPbA0P8supv73wZ-AkAAP__8qOLZw) that Texas used the AI on a failed fourth-and-2 call in the 27-24 loss to Florida on Oct. 17. He said the play showed what the AI "could suggest, not what it actually did."

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]Chris Pappas for Senate

It’s Chris.

It's been an incredible journey since we launched our campaign 18 months
ago, and now everything we’ve worked toward is within reach. We have just
one week until the polls close, the votes are tallied, and we learn who
New Hampshire’s next Senator will be.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_1.w50oPZ&refcode=em20261027-1&t=1003&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]If you’re already on board and ready to help us reach our final,
critical $2 million end-of-month fundraising goal, can I count on you to
rush a $5 contribution before Saturday?

Our final end-of-month deadline is on Saturday. This is our final chance
to build the resources we need to stay competitive with the MAGA
billionaires and national Republican groups propping up John Sununu’s
campaign.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_1.w50oPZ&refcode=em20261027-1&t=1004&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]This is the culmination of everything we have built together — a
movement of people who believe in a freer, fairer future. We set a goal to
raise $2 million before Saturday’s deadline. Can you chip in
$5 before it’s too late?

The GOP and the MAGA billionaires backing John Sununu are determined to
flip this seat red. That’s why they are spending more than $66 million to
try and buy this seat — and they’re counting on us falling short of our
goal.

With Election Day just one week away, every hour counts now. And every
dollar has to stretch even further in these final moments.

That’s why I’m reaching out one last time to ask for your support. Not
because it’s a nice-to-have, but because hitting this goal is the only way
we’ll be able to win this race.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_1.w50oPZ&refcode=em20261027-1&t=1005&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]Please, will you chip in what
you can before our final deadline to help us reach our $2 million
fundraising goal and keep us on track to win on November 3rd?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261027_1.w50oPZ&amount=5&refcode=em20261027-1&t=1024&akid=9804%2E582294%2E9Cln_C ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris Pappas

name: Bernie Sanders
subject: I am, once again, asking for your financial support ...
body:
[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1001&akid=158%2E42639%2ETJoSIb ]Chris Deluzio for PA

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em261027-bernie&refcode2=158.42639.TJoSIb&t=1002&akid=158%2E42639%2ETJoSIb ]Pittsburgh Post Gazette: State, federal lawmakers rally in support of
Allegheny County paid parental leave policy -- Allegheny County Executive
Sara Innamorato was joined by Democratic state and federal officials
Thursday in issuing a call for the county health board to pass
Innamorato’s proposed paid parental leave policy next week. The county
health board is scheduled to vote on the proposal — which would provide 12
weeks of paid parental leave for eligible county residents — on Monday. If
passed, the measure will go before County Council next month. Innamorato,
who is due to give birth to her first child this fall, was joined by
lawmakers including U.S. Reps. Chris Deluzio and Summer Lee, state Reps.
La’Tasha Mayes and Aerion Abney, and state Sen. Nick Pisciottano, at a
press conference at the Western Pennsylvania Diaper Bank in Point Breeze.
“These are elected representatives who don’t just talk about being
pro-family, but are actually willing to step up, to spend political
capital, and to take the action necessary to get pro-family policies
across the finish line,” Innamorato said. Monday’s vote will follow months
of debate on the issue. The policy that goes before the health board has
been revised since the original proposal that would have provided 18 weeks
of paid parental leave. Brought for public comment in May, the initial
plan received mixed reactions from hundreds of county residents who
submitted comments to local officials. In response, the Board of Health
announced sweeping changes to the policy earlier this month, reducing the
length of paid leave to 12 weeks and implementing a small-business cap
that would exempt businesses with fewer than 15 employees. “The county
listened to feedback on the paid parental leave policy and we made several
adjustments,” Innamorato said. More than a dozen states have enacted
mandatory paid parental leave policies, while another nine have adopted
voluntary paid parental leave systems that allow the benefit in the
private insurance market. Pennsylvania has no statewide parental leave
policy, although Sen. Pisciottano, D-Allegheny, introduced legislation in
March that would provide 12 weeks of paid leave to employees who have
worked their jobs for at least a year. That bill was referred to committee
upon introduction but has yet to receive a committee vote or hearing.
Meanwhile, the state House passed a paid family and medical leave bill in
March. That legislation has since stalled in the Republican-controlled
Senate. In June, the Pennsylvania Senate Labor and Industry Committee
voted 9-2 in a bipartisan move to pass the Family Care Act, which would
establish a paid family and medical leave program for up to 20 weeks for
eligible workers for the birth of a child or a serious personal medical
issue. Sponsor Devlin Robinson, R-Allegheny, said the act would fund the
program through employee payroll contributions and be administered by the
state Department of Labor and Industry. The legislation has yet to go to
the Senate floor for a vote. A federal paid parental leave policy — the
FAMILY Act — was introduced in September 2025 and would create a national
paid family and medical leave insurance program. The bill — co-sponsored
by U.S. Reps. Deluzio and Lee, among others — was referred to committee
upon its introduction, but has not advanced to a House floor vote. “Let’s
be honest, this is an issue that should be handled at a federal level,”
Lee said. “We shouldn’t have to be here, county by county, municipality by
municipality, or state by state, ensuring our families are taken care of.”
In lieu of that legislation, Deluzio applauded Innamorato and her
administration for pursuing a paid parental leave policy locally. “When
you go through something as important as starting a family, having a baby,
you shouldn’t be risking your job or your safety to care for yourself and
your baby,” he said. Deluzio said that he supported the recent changes to
the Allegheny County proposed policy made, in part, in response to input
from small business owners. “They were smart,” he said. “They reflected
feedback from the community and small business owners, especially.” State
Rep. La’Tasha Mayes, co-chair of the Black Maternal Health Caucus, said
most mothers, about 60%, return to work within three months of giving
birth — many within six to eight weeks. “You bring a baby into the world
and then you must return to work,” she said. “Your life has changed. Your
mind has changed. Your body has changed. Your thoughts should be about how
you heal and how you take care of your new baby, but the competing
thoughts are, ‘I’ve got to get back to work.’” Mayes said the policy would
ultimately help prevent maternal deaths, particularly for Black women who
have a significantly higher rate of maternal mortality than the national
average, and two and a half times higher than their white counterparts,
according to the county health department. Nationally, the CDC found that
the U.S. maternal mortality rate was 17.9 deaths per 100,000 live births
in 2024.

Sisters and Brothers –

The political future of our country rests upon one very simple principle:
the need for working people to stand together and fight back against
corporate greed, and create an economy that works for all of us, and not
just billionaires and large corporations.

So when we have progressive candidates with the guts to take on corporate
power in this country, we have to do what we can to support them if we are
going to have any chance at transforming this country and creating a
government that works for all of us.

One of those people is Congressman Chris Deluzio in Pennsylvania.

Chris understands that our current healthcare system is broken and wildly
expensive. He believes, as I do, that healthcare is a human right, not a
privilege, and that we must end the embarrassment of being the only major
country on earth that does not guarantee healthcare to every man, woman
and child. That is why he supports Medicare for All.

Chris understands that we have a corrupt campaign finance system which
allows the very rich and their super PACs to buy and sell politicians.
That is why he fights vigorously to end the disastrous Citizens United
Supreme Court decision — which allows Big Money to control our political
process.

Chris understands that too many workers in America are earning starvation
wages. That is why he fights to raise the minimum wage to a living wage,
to make it easier for workers to join unions, to build the millions of
units of low income and affordable housing this country desperately needs
and make sure that seniors can retire with dignity and security.

Sisters and brothers, Chris' campaign is about more than just one single
House seat. His work is about taking on the powerful special interests
that dominate our economic and political life.

And keeping him in Congress requires all of us to do our part to make it
happen. And that is why I am once again asking for your financial support.

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em261027-bernie&t=1003&akid=158%2E42639%2ETJoSIb ]Please contribute $27 or whatever you can afford to Chris Deluzio's
campaign for Congress in Pennsylvania. I intend to do my part, but it will
take all of us. Not just me. Us.

clean_body: [ ]Chris Deluzio for PA [ ]Pittsburgh Post Gazette: State, federal lawmakers rally in support of Allegheny County paid parental leave policy -- Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato was joined by Democratic state and federal officials Thursday in issuing a call for the county health board to pass Innamorato’s proposed paid parental leave policy next week. The county health board is scheduled to vote on the proposal — which would provide 12 weeks of paid parental leave for eligible county residents — on Monday. If passed, the measure will go before County Council next month. Innamorato, who is due to give birth to her first child this fall, was joined by lawmakers including U.S. Reps. Chris Deluzio and Summer Lee, state Reps. La’Tasha Mayes and Aerion Abney, and state Sen. Nick Pisciottano, at a press conference at the Western Pennsylvania Diaper Bank in Point Breeze. “These are elected representatives who don’t just talk about being pro-family, but are actually willing to step up, to spend political capital, and to take the action necessary to get pro-family policies across the finish line,” Innamorato said. Monday’s vote will follow months of debate on the issue. The policy that goes before the health board has been revised since the original proposal that would have provided 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Brought for public comment in May, the initial plan received mixed reactions from hundreds of county residents who submitted comments to local officials. In response, the Board of Health announced sweeping changes to the policy earlier this month, reducing the length of paid leave to 12 weeks and implementing a small-business cap that would exempt businesses with fewer than 15 employees. “The county listened to feedback on the paid parental leave policy and we made several adjustments,” Innamorato said. More than a dozen states have enacted mandatory paid parental leave policies, while another nine have adopted voluntary paid parental leave systems that allow the benefit in the private insurance market. Pennsylvania has no statewide parental leave policy, although Sen. Pisciottano, D-Allegheny, introduced legislation in March that would provide 12 weeks of paid leave to employees who have worked their jobs for at least a year. That bill was referred to committee upon introduction but has yet to receive a committee vote or hearing. Meanwhile, the state House passed a paid family and medical leave bill in March. That legislation has since stalled in the Republican-controlled Senate. In June, the Pennsylvania Senate Labor and Industry Committee voted 9-2 in a bipartisan move to pass the Family Care Act, which would establish a paid family and medical leave program for up to 20 weeks for eligible workers for the birth of a child or a serious personal medical issue. Sponsor Devlin Robinson, R-Allegheny, said the act would fund the program through employee payroll contributions and be administered by the state Department of Labor and Industry. The legislation has yet to go to the Senate floor for a vote. A federal paid parental leave policy — the FAMILY Act — was introduced in September 2025 and would create a national paid family and medical leave insurance program. The bill — co-sponsored by U.S. Reps. Deluzio and Lee, among others — was referred to committee upon its introduction, but has not advanced to a House floor vote. “Let’s be honest, this is an issue that should be handled at a federal level,” Lee said. “We shouldn’t have to be here, county by county, municipality by municipality, or state by state, ensuring our families are taken care of.” In lieu of that legislation, Deluzio applauded Innamorato and her administration for pursuing a paid parental leave policy locally. “When you go through something as important as starting a family, having a baby, you shouldn’t be risking your job or your safety to care for yourself and your baby,” he said. Deluzio said that he supported the recent changes to the Allegheny County proposed policy made, in part, in response to input from small business owners. “They were smart,” he said. “They reflected feedback from the community and small business owners, especially.” State Rep. La’Tasha Mayes, co-chair of the Black Maternal Health Caucus, said most mothers, about 60%, return to work within three months of giving birth — many within six to eight weeks. “You bring a baby into the world and then you must return to work,” she said. “Your life has changed. Your mind has changed. Your body has changed. Your thoughts should be about how you heal and how you take care of your new baby, but the competing thoughts are, ‘I’ve got to get back to work.’” Mayes said the policy would ultimately help prevent maternal deaths, particularly for Black women who have a significantly higher rate of maternal mortality than the national average, and two and a half times higher than their white counterparts, according to the county health department. Nationally, the CDC found that the U.S. maternal mortality rate was 17.9 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2024. # Talarico v. Paxton
| |
---
|
---
Medical liberty is on the ballot this General Election, and the race for U.S. Senate deserves your attention. **Actual records speak louder than campaign rhetoric** , and the contrast of James Talarico and Ken Paxton could not be bigger: **_JAMES TALARICO: SIDES WITH BIG PHARMA_** Talarico has served in the Texas House since 2019. During that time, he has **repeatedly voted against medical liberty protections**. When lawmakers considered measures to prohibit vaccine-based discrimination, defend informed consent, and hold pharmaceutical companies accountable, **Talarico voted against those protections** (and several others!) every single time. He simply has not met a Pharma-backed bill he didn’t love. **_KEN PAXTON: DEFENDS MEDICAL LIBERTY_** When medical liberty is threatened, Ken Paxton has **time and time again used his office to challenge Big Pharma** , defend patient rights, and investigate conflicts of interest influencing childhood vaccine recommendations. And **HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. agrees!** At last week’s campaign stop in Fort Worth, Secretary Kennedy said he needs Paxton in D.C. to “challenge official orthodoxies and vested interests.” During his time as Attorney General, **Paxton****fearlessly stood in the trenches with TFVC** , and has even asked us for expert collaboration on investigations his office was conducting. You owe it to yourself and the future of medical freedom in Texas to know where these candidates stand before you vote. **Texas needs champions for medical liberty in positions of power at every level.** Before you head to the polls, study the record, and use the [**TFVC Voter Guide**](https://xdzgmz.clicks.mlsend.com/gw/c/v2.k1._YK2dWPKOgYMw1aDdTUl_ENiQDu2tDinaBZDZKtCRtb2Fvs7hnmQyNgIwQbTN3rhA_qS-OuVEshMglEM2UB2lMaUB7yc79IlC48O8x8UeWZyUYu0QFT7QrpPZo8VMqxFLqnlmkSV-xOoA3-JcnEL3OOnQ75lwUh8STRNpsNzOE_1lVrmIRAI_2m1krEq1ad4wMEwpZ6VcA32N-ONGZKwM4Sb2--uu6J-TYSfBa6895ZqOhF7NEgDvndr5MZZYAWkls_feOEGZ4_iyR1zfD6aaldotAfkcohVuqNN7L-BQ5A034Ks3Ho0KNaOBAbUrRa8ahYgPs5bIX3ikL5fijB41ng7NQAL58u_0hRxPRIhpLkqulQXgJLNAjuTR5fjYcOgCz3Efd8XdhsPeuFJdCCryPPpq5mle3JYDDKqyEUfL_HsiAVCYIKbp_8obNQ5zvcr9W8HF5NtUUl8ZLoHJl_wf1Dg6v8EkBmi0ay-MXDmcCUhNY3fqqRIx3s9c9QpI09UET6-gVZQbmlLT3JWRfzcgs0lu1I3baDVtGWy_bg) to make informed choices all the way down your ballot. **Every race and vote counts!**

During that time, he has repeatedly voted against medical liberty protections. When lawmakers considered measures to prohibit vaccine-based discrimination, defend informed consent, and hold pharmaceutical companies accountable, Talarico voted against those protections (and several others!) every single time. He simply has not met a Pharma-backed bill he didn’t love. KEN PAXTON: DEFENDS MEDICAL LIBERTY When medical liberty is threatened, Ken Paxton has time and time again used his office to challenge Big Pharma , defend patient rights, and investigate conflicts of interest influencing childhood vaccine recommendations. And HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. agrees! At last week’s campaign stop in Fort Worth, Secretary Kennedy said he needs Paxton in D.C. to “challenge official orthodoxies and vested interests.” During his time as Attorney General, Paxtonfearlessly stood in the trenches with TFVC , and has even asked us for expert collaboration on investigations his office was conducting. You owe it to yourself and the future of medical freedom in Texas to know where these candidates stand before you vote. Texas needs champions for medical liberty in positions of power at every level. Fellow Patriot,
I was a freshman at West Point when the Twin Towers fell.
None of us who were there will ever forget that morning. We'd signed up to serve a country at peace. By that afternoon, every cadet in my class knew we'd be going to war.
Not one of us flinched.
Over nine combat tours in Afghanistan and Iraq, I flew the Apache attack helicopter and then MH-47G Chinooks with the 160th SOAR "Night Stalkers," carrying special operators into places most Americans will never see. I did it because I love this country more than I love my own life. Every man on those birds felt the same way.
**And I’m still committed to fighting for this country today – but what I see happening here at home terrifies me.**
_Here 's why._
America has never been beaten from the outside. After Pearl Harbor, we rallied and won a world war. After 9/11, we took the fight to the terrorists who attacked us. Give our warfighters what they need and put them on any battlefield against any enemy on earth – and we win.
Abraham Lincoln understood this almost 200 years ago. He said the danger to America would never come from abroad. "If destruction be our lot," he warned, "we must ourselves be its author and finisher."
**That 's exactly what the radical Left is doing. Brick by brick, they're tearing America down from the inside.**
**_Our sovereignty?_** They threw open our southern border and allowed cartels to smuggle in dangerous drugs and criminals. They voted against requiring proof of citizenship to vote. A nation that can't control who comes in or who casts its ballots isn't a nation for long.
**_Our culture?_** They sneer at the flag, the troops, and the Constitution those troops swore to defend. Faith, family and hard work – the things that built this country – they treat as something to be ashamed of.
**_And our kids?_** That's what keeps me up at night. The Left wants our children taught that America is rotten to the core. That the greatest gift they'll ever receive – being born American – is something to apologize for.
A generation that's taught to hate its country won't defend it. And the socialists know it.
Today's Democratic Party isn't the party your parents knew. Socialists from the DSA wing are running the show now. And the so-called moderate, pro-America Democrats? They've had every chance to stand up to this monster. They've proven they either won't or can't.
_So it 's up to us._
**And in just a matter of days, the socialists have a real shot at taking back the House.**
Our majority is razor-thin. Democrats don't need a wave – they need to flip just a handful of seats. **Every single race in the country is on the table, and they 're pouring money into all of them at once.**
If they pull it off, Hakeem Jeffries gets the gavel. And the socialists get the keys.

You know what comes next. Endless witch hunts. Impeachment circuses. Every bill to secure the border and protect our elections will be dead on arrival. Two more years of the Left fighting to undo everything we've accomplished – and setting the stage to finish the job in 2028.
**This is the whole ballgame. Not one race._The entire House._**
I know that fight better than most. Last December, when our majority was on the line in Tennessee's special election, national Democrats threw everything they had at it. We beat them by nearly 9 points. Now they want revenge – on me and on every Republican standing between them and power.
**In just a matter of days, it all comes down to Election Day.** The Democrats and their media allies are watching every close race for a Republican who looks weak. Wherever they see weakness, they'll pile on. Wherever they see strength, they'll think twice.
_That 's why I'm coming to you directly._
**I 'm asking you to stand in the gap over these next few days – because right now, the House is the line, and we need patriots holding it.**

The country's on the line and the threat is coming from within. That’s why I'm asking you to answer the call with me – for our sovereignty, for our way of life and for the kids who deserve to inherit the same America we did.
**Please don 't wait. The clock is running.**
For God and country,
Matt Van Epps

Two more years of the Left fighting to undo everything we've accomplished – and setting the stage to finish the job in 2028. This is the whole ballgame. Not one race.The entire House. I know that fight better than most. Last December, when our majority was on the line in Tennessee's special election, national Democrats threw everything they had at it. We beat them by nearly 9 points. Now they want revenge – on me and on every Republican standing between them and power. In just a matter of days, it all comes down to Election Day. The Democrats and their media allies are watching every close race for a Republican who looks weak. Wherever they see weakness, they'll pile on. Wherever they see strength, they'll think twice. That 's why I'm coming to you directly. I 'm asking you to stand in the gap over these next few days – because right now, the House is the line, and we need patriots holding it. The country's on the line and the threat is coming from within. That’s why I'm asking you to answer the call with me – for our sovereignty, for our way of life and for the kids who deserve to inherit the same America we did. Please don 't wait. The clock is running. For God and country, Matt Van Epps P.S. America has never been beaten from the outside – only we can destroy her. body:
Because this isn't easy. It's an absolute dogfight, and you have to love the fight, really love it, to keep pushing when the odds are stacked against you.

| Please don't take my appreciation for granted, Friend.The love I have for you, for Minnesota, and for this country. How many people can say they've put everything on the line and have been within striking distance of making history by flipping Minnesota - a Democrat stronghold - to the Republican column?Not many. Because this isn't easy. It's an absolute dogfight, and you have to love the fight, really love it, to keep pushing when the odds are stacked against you.That's exactly what I've done. And I'm not backing down now.I've dedicated everything I have to flipping the US Senate seat in Minnesota, and there is no question in my mind that this is the right choice when I've seen first-hand what Peggy Flanagan and Tim Walz have done. All the rampant fraud that took place here occurred under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as under Tim Walz. It's time to drop the axe, show Peggy the door, and restore common sense to Minnesota for good. [The only question now is if you'll join me. ](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckTFv3TAMhH-NvMmQKFnyGzwUCNwu6dCl6CSwFu0ItSVDpl_y_n3hBN2LjDwcPvKOP5_DM6Y15eU7bjQsZd9DPcK-Eh4US2bGP7Q9cN8rTQk5gAIntZLgA06c7hQsNnGw6KxzrqFB-5vRqtOgm5dhckhd382g7Gwna34r1JoM-ls03nrdpOECagVeg-30rQWv-5vzsXeuN25GYRXFxKW2122VjhQpc8K1ncrWrMML834I80XAKGA8aDorta8pV4qXQ8DIOJcHyrlUeVBGJgHjNTzK-S5uKWc6CqPEHN-VclY5lTNzfVxYM9YLW1NehHniepIAd_IWJtx2TEsW5ukjhTbh6zf560erdQ--Cwyqc8oqabUyAhy9BU7xv-1vZ75fG-_yyi7_NdXUIe6vaV3T4bywatkwfdTBn33gfYC_AQAA__-8U6S1)Look, I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said.That's why I'm humbly asking you for $15. Not $500. Not even $50. | | In our everyday lives, we need a photo ID to buy cough syrup and to get on an airplane—**we should also need a photo ID to vote.** This is why one of my top priorities in Congress is strengthening election integrity. To protect the ballot box, my goal is to re-implement the need for three forms of ID to register to vote, alongside a strict requirement for a photo ID at the polling booth. .By implementing these basic, common-sense measures, the impact will be clear and immediate: it **ensures that only eligible voters are participating in the democratic process.** We must secure our elections, so they remain fair and truly representative of our hardworking citizens. I will confidently fight for these essential reforms in Washington to restore faith in our system and guarantee that every legal vote is protected.

| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | **Modernizing Women’s Healthcare: Putting Patients First and Protecting Taxpayer Dollars**.Recently, NBC News reported that the President and First Lady signed an executive order establishing a new Women’s Health Division at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) alongside a White House Women’s Health Task Force led by the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Chief of Staff. **Aiming to close research gaps and modernize care, the initiative also highlights the need to improve the access and affordability of healthcare for women across the nation.** Furthermore, the administration has moved to cut wasteful NIH grants on diversity-related topics, align federal Title X family planning funds with pro-family priorities, and conduct a vital safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone..These federal efforts address critical issues affecting families right here in Illinois' 6th Congressional District. Niki Conforti supports the actions the HHS Secretary is taking to improve public health policy, believing that federal health entities must focus strictly on objective science and transparency rather than publicly funded advocacy. **For far too long, Democrat-championed policies like Obamacare have been a disaster for Illinois, shrinking consumer choices to just two options in many counties and causing healthcare costs to skyrocket over the last decade.** Instead of fighting to make healthcare affordable for his constituents, incumbent Democrat Sean Casten has focused on partisan messaging and pushing a radical abortion agenda—including despicable support for taxpayer-funded and late-term abortions that directly opposes the values of his constituents. .**Having spent 12 years in healthcare leadership roles, Niki Conforti brings invaluable industry experience to the table and maintains a strict "district-first" mentality.** When elected to Congress, Niki will build on these federal reforms and fight for the hardworking families of the 6th District. Niki will look at policies, such as: .
* **Lowering Healthcare Costs Through Transparency:** Pushing for real reform that enforces strict transparency in medical billing, eliminating surprise bills and fostering free-market competition among healthcare systems to naturally drive down prices for patients.
* **Expanding Consumer Choice and Flexibility:** Consumers deserve more options in the marketplace. Niki supports allowing families to purchase and transport health insurance policies across state lines and expanding Health Savings Accounts (HSAs).
* **Protecting Life and Taxpayer Dollars:** Proudly Pro-Life with exceptions for rape, incest, and the life of the mother, Niki will fiercely oppose the Democrats' radical abortion agenda.
* **Eliminating Bureaucratic Waste and DEI Mandates:** Downsizing bloated federal bureaucracies, dismantling divisive DEI practices in the federal government, and conducting rigorous audits to root out the waste and fraud draining our national treasury.
* **Evaluating AI with a District-First Approach:** As new technologies like artificial intelligence are utilized to speed up medical discoveries, Niki believes AI should be regulated by the federal government using a "district-first" approach—evaluating policies by whether they truly protect and benefit local workers, families, and patients.

. It is time to **replace a broken, unaffordable system with sensible solutions** that empower women and families, protect the unborn, and deliver true healthcare affordability. .

clean_body: Together, we can build an economy where hard work pays off and where everyone has a shot at a decent life. | | | Friend, with Election Day just days away, I’ve been reflecting on why I got in this race. I was guided by a simple principle: When you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work. And yet, I’ve seen Ohioans working harder than ever and still being left behind while Washington politicians give handout after handout to billionaires and corporate special interests. I didn’t plan to run for office again. But I couldn’t sit on the sidelines while Jon Husted and politicians like him in Washington kept failing the people of Ohio. This campaign has never been about left versus right. It’s about who you fight for – and who you’re willing to stand up to. When we fought to save the pensions of tens of thousands of Ohio retirees, we stood up to Wall Street and won. When we fought to cap insulin prices and bring down the cost of prescription drugs, we stood up to Big Pharma and won. I knew a campaign founded on the idea of unrigging the system for working folks had the legs to win. This movement we’ve created has been truly incredible – and it’s all thanks to supporters like you. But I’m in the fight of my life to flip this seat, and this final stretch is incredibly tough. The GOP and its right-wing billionaire donors are spending millions to mislead voters and attack me, and the only way I can fight back and win is with your grassroots support. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately Sherrod Brown and Judicial Action Network. Thank you for standing with me until the very end. With Election Day exactly one week away, I wanted to share an update on my race against Andy Barr and ask for your support.
Trump and his allies are pouring _millions_ into Kentucky to protect their grip on power. Attack ads are flooding the airwaves, and they're doing everything they can to drown out our Kentucky-first message.
But we're not backing down.
My opponent and I are tied in the polls. **This is the most competitive race Kentucky has seen in a generation, and we cannot afford to take a single vote for granted.

** We need to reach as many Kentucky voters as possible before they head to the polls in just _one week._ That means making sure they hear directly from me, not just the attacks funded by Trump and his deep-pocketed allies.
Unlike Andy, I'm not relying on Trump and wealthy special interests to fund this campaign. I'm relying on people like you who believe Kentucky deserves better.
**With just 7 days left, will you make a contribution today to help us reach voters and bring this race across the finish line?**
[ Make a donation to my Senate Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/a92a4a5e-e4ff-4bb8-a81b-8edcb9ab4bd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Make a recurring donation](https://substack.com/redirect/878f5f90-51d2-40ca-b47c-555c801d41e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you.
Charles Booker

name: Citizens Alliance New Hampshire
subject: What's your plan for Tuesday?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire, Dan Gray, Treasurer, 45 Lafayette Rd
body:
We have one week to get voters to the polls on Election Day...

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/FHCiANHuSob?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | | | | | Peter,

**We have seven days...**

That’s all that stands between now and the election that will decide who will fight for our New Hampshire values in Concord.

I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again...**We cannot afford to sit this one out.**

If we do not show up next Tuesday, November 3, our legislature will be filled with radical extremists who will sell out our values, our freedom, and our way of life every chance they get.

Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire has done our homework. We spoke with the candidates. We learned where they stand. **That is why we have officially endorsed 155 liberty champions who have signed The Pledge** and made a public promise to fight for you.
[**See our full list of endorsed candidates by clicking here!**](https://us.list-manage.com/ckkSF33Y9Gv?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
---
[|

| [SPONSOR A LIBERTY DOOR KNOCKER FOR $175 IN THE FINAL STRETCH >>>](https://us.list-manage.com/15NIhGgC12h?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
---
| | **We have one week to get voters to the polls on Election Day.**

Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire has teams on the ground knocking doors and speaking with voters about these important races, but we need all hands on deck.

**If you want to help Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire knock more doors before polls close on Tuesday, you can go to:** [www.CitizensAllianceNH.org/donate](https://us.list-manage.com/7xwkL4IjS8s?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) **and sponsor a doorknocker for $175!**

If you’ve already donated, start a group chat with your friends, family members, neighbors, and coworkers and encourage them to make a plan to vote next week.

**If we want a legislature that represents our Live Free or Die state, we have to show up next week.

**Mark your calendar. Make your plan. Talk to the people around you.

Then get to the polls next Tuesday, November 3, and vote for the [Pledge Signers](https://us.list-manage.com/XqjWQLH8t0o?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) who will stand for liberty.

We look forward to seeing you at the polls.

LET’S WIN!

If you only read one email from me this month, please make it this one.

As a pastor, I learned something early: _you can’t ask people to show up after the doors have closed._

Right now, the doors are about to close on our **LAST End-of-Month deadline** before the Midterm elections on November 3rd.

After that, there are no more reports. No more chances to catch up. _**Just Election Day, and whatever we have in hand.**_

And what we have in hand will decide whether North Carolina has the resources to hold the line, and whether Republicans keep the Majority.

That’s not me being dramatic. _It’s the math of this election._

clean_body: One week from now, they will make history One week from now, they will make history | ~~ | | Peter, One week from today, the polls close on an election that has never happened before in American history: five Indigenous women on one ballot — three of them running for top statewide offices. Mary Peltola , a Yup'ik leader, leads the Alaska Senate race forecasters call the "majority maker" — and she just counterpunched a DOJ lawsuit designed to block her win. Peggy Flanagan is in a slight lead for the seat that would make her the first Native American woman EVER in the U.S. Senate. And Donald Trump himself just said last night that if she wins, he will call it fraudulent. Deb Haaland is defending her lead to become the first Native American woman ever elected governor — in a state that barred her people from voting until 1948. Sharice Davids and Claire Valdez are fighting for the House seats a Democratic majority runs through. All five are tied or ahead. All five races get decided by what happens in the next seven days. This is the sprint to run the final ads, knock the final doors, and reach every last voter. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ With gratitude, Indigenous Women Lead PAC | Paid for by Indigenous Women Lead PAC Indigenous Women Lead PACPO Box 15845Washington, DC 20003United States

On Friday night, I was joined by Governor Josh Stein and Justice Anita Earls for an amazing Get Out The Vote concert. We heard from North Carolina musical artists Davie Circle, Karly Hartzman, Tift Merritt, Hiss Golden Messenger and Watchhouse x Viv & Riley!
Get Out The Vote Concert!
More than a thousand people spent their Friday night supporting our campaign, hearing about the stakes of this election and listening to some great artists. With just 7 days until Election Day, now is the time for folks across the state to grab a friend and head to the polls to cast their ballots.
Working families need a change and I'm ready to bring some North Carolina common sense to Washington DC to make stuff cost less. subject: How Maine helps us get a majority

body:
Chip in before Election Day

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3067%2E4032634%2E2mPDjL)
---
Just over a week ago, I stood with my friend Troy Jackson in Portland, looking out at about a thousand Mainers. You could feel it in that crowd. People are tired of watching billionaires and Trump’s corruption. They’re ready to take their country back, and they want a government that works for them. Sound familiar? It’s not just happening in Maine. I’ve heard the same thing in every state I’ve visited this year: in town halls, at kitchen tables, and from crowds just like the one in Portland. Americans everywhere are ready for change. That’s why what happens in Maine matters so much. The road to a Senate majority depends on it. And with a majority, we can hold Trump’s administration accountable, block his extreme judges, and pass policies that lower costs for working families. Susan Collins has spent 30 years in Washington. Troy Jackson has spent his life in northern Maine, working as a logger and fighting for working families as a union man. He knows what it’s like to work hard and still struggle to get ahead, and he’s spent his career taking on powerful interests — and winning. **The choice couldn’t be clearer.** [**We have one week left to help Troy get across the finish line. Every contribution can help his campaign reach voters and make the case for change before they cast their ballots. Please split a donation between Troy Jackson’s campaign and our movement today.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3883?t=8&akid=3067%2E4032634%2E2mPDjL)

Yesterday, we launched our final end-of-month fund before Election Day — one of our last, best chances to support EMILYs List women. This is the moment we’ve been working toward all year. Our candidates have gained momentum in some of the toughest, closest races in the country — and it’s all because of this community. Now, we’re asking for your support one last time. We’re raising $500,000 before the end of October to support the women who can take back power from state houses to the U.S. House. We’ve set an ambitious goal to raise $500,000 by October 31 to support our full slate of Democratic pro-choice women in the final days before Election Day. We know that’s a lot to raise in less than a week. But we've seen this community rise to the occasion time and time again — and with so much on the line, we're counting on you to do it once more. = = At the beginning of this year, we set three ambitious goals: build Democratic power in the states, elect our largest-ever roster of EMILYs List women to the U.S. House, and help build the path to a Democratic U.S. Senate majority. Friends and Neighbors,
Yevgeny “Eugene” Vindman fled the Soviet Union as a kid.
But Yevgeny just announced he’s bringing _**Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez,**_ the face of the modern American socialist movement for a GOTV rally in Prince William County.
_**Think about that for a second.**_
In a district full of military families, small-business owners, and people who just want their electric bills and grocery prices to stop climbing, the best Yevgeny can do is fly in the congresswoman who once said the world would end in 12 years if we didn’t ban fossil fuels, championed the Green New “Scam,” and treats the border like a suggestion.
_**This is Yevgeny’s cry for help.**_
While Yevgeny is busy importing national progressive celebrities and dodging basic questions about not denouncing socialism, running this campaign the old fashion way: talking to actual voters across the district about energy, affordability, border security, and results.
_**He can have AOC. We’ll take the district.**_
Election Day is November 3. Every dollar we raise this week goes straight into the ground game that counters the circus coming to town Friday night.

Let’s send Yevgeny packing.
[**Chip in $25, $50, or $100 if you can.**](https://us.list-manage.com/4R7V1wa8glG?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)

One team. One fight.

**TUESDAY, OCTOBER 27, 2026**
**Benjamin Franklin | Autobiography**
"But mark how luxury will enter families, and make a progress, in spite of principle."
Benjamin Franklin wrote this after discovering that his wife, Deborah, had replaced his ordinary breakfast bowl and spoon with china and silver. As Franklin recounted it, she thought he deserved what his neighbors had.
Franklin saw a departure from frugality. Deborah saw something her husband deserved.
It was only a bowl and a spoon. Yet beneath this small domestic disagreement lay a question that reaches into almost every household: What happens when the principles we live by meet the people we love?
Perhaps the test of a principle is not only how firmly we hold it, but how we understand it when someone we love looks at it from a different angle.
**Pause.
Breath.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

James

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261027-1-ak&t=1051&akid=1144%2E1347274%2EGdvrRG ]'New York Times: In Texas, Talarico Inspires a Recurring Blue-Tinted
Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
